draft.title: Equivalent fractions and comparing fractions
card: Equivalent fractions have the same value. Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number to make one.
To compare two fractions, rewrite them with the same denominator. Then the fraction with the larger numerator is larger.
Example: compare \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(\frac{5}{6}\). A common denominator is 12. \(\frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{12}\) and \(\frac{5}{6} = \frac{10}{12}\), so \(\frac{5}{6}\) is larger.
draft.remember: Do the same to the top and bottom to keep the value. Same denominator, then compare numerators.

a.q: Mei multiplies the top and bottom of \(\frac{4}{7}\) by the same number. Which fraction could she get?
a.why: Multiplying the top and bottom of \(\frac{4}{7}\) by 3 gives \(\frac{12}{21}\). \(\frac{7}{10}\) is tempting because 3 was added to both numbers, but adding does not keep the value.
a.clue: Look for the same number used on the top and bottom.

b.q: Ravi ate \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a pizza and Zoe ate \(\frac{3}{4}\) of an identical pizza. Who ate more, and why?
b.why: With a common denominator of 12, Ravi ate \(\frac{8}{12}\) and Zoe ate \(\frac{9}{12}\). Zoe ate more. Comparing only the denominators is a mistake, because it ignores the numerators.
b.clue: Write both fractions with a denominator of 12.

proposal.title: Equivalent fractions and comparing fractions
card: Equivalent fractions have the same value. To make one, multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number.
For example, \(\frac{2}{3} = \frac{2 \times 4}{3 \times 4}\), which is \(\frac{8}{12}\). Dividing works too: \(\frac{10}{15} = \frac{10 \div 5}{15 \div 5}\), which is \(\frac{2}{3}\).
To compare two fractions, rewrite them with the same denominator. Then the fraction with the larger numerator is larger.
Example: compare \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(\frac{5}{6}\). A common denominator is 12. \(\frac{3}{4} = \frac{9}{12}\) and \(\frac{5}{6} = \frac{10}{12}\), so \(\frac{5}{6}\) is larger.
proposal.remember: Multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number. To compare, match the denominators, then compare numerators.

a.q: Mei multiplies the top and bottom of \(\frac{4}{7}\) by the same number. Which fraction could she get?
a.why: Multiplying the top and bottom of \(\frac{4}{7}\) by 3 gives \(\frac{12}{21}\). \(\frac{7}{10}\) is tempting because 3 was added to both numbers, but adding does not keep the value.
a.clue: Look for the same number used to multiply the top and bottom.

b.q: Ravi ate \(\frac{2}{3}\) of a pizza and Zoe ate \(\frac{3}{4}\) of an identical pizza. Who ate more, and why?
opts: Neither, as each is one piece short of a whole
b.why: With a common denominator of 12, Ravi ate \(\frac{8}{12}\) and Zoe ate \(\frac{9}{12}\), so Zoe ate more. Comparing only the denominators is a mistake, because it ignores the numerators. The pieces are different sizes, so being one piece short does not make them equal.
b.clue: Write both fractions with a denominator of 12.
